C1.name: Changed bank details for a known supplier ABN
C1.description: Compares the invoice's BSB and account with the accounts you've paid this supplier (same ABN) before. A new account for a known supplier is the classic invoice-scam move.
C1.plain_name: New bank account for a known supplier
C1.plain: Is this a different bank account from the one you've always paid this supplier? The number one sign of invoice fraud.

C2.name: Flag register hit (account/PayID/ABN/email)
C2.description: Looks up the account, PayID, ABN and email in the bank's register of details already reported in scams.
C2.plain: Have these bank details, ABN or email already been reported in a scam?

C3.name: Confirmation of Payee result
C3.description: The bank's existing Confirmation of Payee result (Westpac Verify): does the account name match who holds the account?
C3.plain: Does the name on the bank account match the business you think you're paying?

C4.name: New payee + high amount
C4.description: First payment to this payee, weighted up when the amount is large. New isn't bad on its own, but it removes the safety of history.
C4.plain: You've never paid this account before. Not bad on its own, but there's no history to lean on.

C5.name: Invoice hash / template seen before (fraud or duplicate)
C5.description: Fingerprints the PDF and its layout to spot an invoice or template already seen in a reported scam, or one you've already paid.
C5.plain: Is this exact invoice, or its template, already known from a scam or a past payment?

C6.name: Duplicate invoice number or amount
C6.description: Same invoice number or amount as one already paid to this supplier: a duplicate payment or a recycled fake.
C6.plain: Have you already paid an invoice with this number or amount?

C7.name: Amount anomaly vs supplier history
C7.description: Compares the amount with what you usually pay this supplier. Far above the usual (over 3× the median) is unusual.
C7.plain: Is the amount far higher than you normally pay this supplier?

C8.name: ABN checksum (mod 89)
C8.description: Runs the official ABN checksum. A made-up ABN fails it instantly, before any lookup.
C8.plain: ABNs have a built-in maths check. A made-up ABN usually fails it.

C9.name: ACN checksum
C9.description: Runs the ACN checksum for company numbers printed on the invoice.
C9.plain: The same built-in maths check, for company numbers (ACN).

C10.name: GST maths and tax-invoice validity
C10.description: Recalculates GST (10% of the taxable subtotal) and the total. Sloppy fakes often get the maths wrong.
C10.plain: Is the GST 10% and do the totals add up? Rushed fakes often get the maths wrong.

C11.name: BSB validity and bank-name match (AusPayNet)
C11.description: Checks the BSB exists in the AusPayNet directory and belongs to the bank the invoice names.
C11.plain: Does the BSB exist, and does it belong to the bank the invoice names?

C12.name: PDF metadata (online editor, mod ≫ create date)
C12.description: Reads PDF metadata: which app made it, and whether it was modified long after creation or by an online editor.
C12.plain: Was the PDF made by normal invoicing software, or changed later in an online editor?

C13.name: Incremental updates editing payment fields
C13.description: Looks for later edits saved on top of the original PDF that touch the payment fields. Strong evidence of tampering.
C13.plain_name: PDF edited after it was made
C13.plain: Were the payment details changed in a later edit saved on top of the original PDF?

C14.name: Hidden text, zero-width chars, homoglyphs
C14.description: Finds text a person can't see: white or tiny text, zero-width characters, look-alike letters. Often instructions aimed at AI.
C14.plain: Is there text a person can't see, like white or tiny writing, often aimed at tricking AI?

C15.name: Overlay or annotation over the bank details
C15.description: Detects new text or boxes drawn over the original bank details, a common way to alter a genuine invoice.
C15.plain_name: Something drawn over the bank details
C15.plain: Has new text or a box been pasted over the original bank details?

C16.name: Embedded JS, launch actions, odd links
C16.description: Flags embedded scripts, auto-launch actions or odd links inside the PDF.
C16.plain: Does the PDF contain scripts, auto-run actions or odd links?

C17.name: Structured extraction + internal consistency
C17.description: AI reads the invoice into structured fields (supplier, ABN, amounts, bank details) and code checks they agree with each other. Most Tier 1 checks depend on it.
C17.plain: AI pulls out the supplier, ABN, amounts and bank details, and code checks they agree with each other.

C18.name: Payment-method inconsistency (BPAY vs BSB, two accounts)
C18.description: Payment details that contradict themselves: says BPAY but gives a BSB, or lists two different accounts.
C18.plain: Do the payment details disagree, like two different accounts on one invoice?

C19.name: "Bank details have changed" language
C19.description: Wording like "our bank details have changed". Weighted up when the account really has changed.
C19.plain: Does the invoice say the bank details have changed? Scammers often warn you first.

C20.name: Urgency / pressure / secrecy language
C20.description: Pressure language: pay within 24 hours, urgent, don't call, keep this confidential.
C20.plain: Is there pressure: pay today, urgent, don't call us, keep this quiet?

C21.name: ABN Lookup: active, name match, entity type
C21.description: Official ABN Lookup: is the ABN active, and does the registered name match the supplier on the invoice?
C21.plain_name: ABN is active and the name matches
C21.plain: On the official ABN register, is the ABN active and does the name match the supplier?

C22.name: GST charged but not GST-registered
C22.description: Invoice charges GST but the ABN isn't registered for GST.
C22.plain: The invoice charges GST, but the business isn't registered for GST.

C23.name: ABN age vs claimed history
C23.description: How long the ABN has existed compared with how established the business claims to be.
C23.plain: Has the ABN existed as long as the business claims?

C24.name: Real ABN, but payee or email belongs to someone else
C24.description: The ABN is real, but the account name or email belongs to someone else: a real business being impersonated.
C24.plain: The ABN is real, but the bank account or email belongs to someone else: a real business being impersonated.

C25.name: ATO / government official payment-details allowlist
C25.description: Invoices claiming to be the ATO or government must use the official published payment details. Anything else is a hard stop.
C25.plain: Invoices claiming to be from the ATO or government must use the official payment details.

C26.name: Contact consistency (email vs website domain, free-mail, area code)
C26.description: Do the email, website and phone fit together? Free-mail addresses and mismatched domains are weak warning signs.
C26.plain: Do the email, website and phone number belong together? A Gmail address for a company is a weak warning sign.

C27.name: Directory / domain-renewal offer disguised as invoice
C27.description: Spots directory listings or domain renewals dressed up as invoices for services you never ordered.
C27.plain: Is this a sales offer, like a directory listing or domain renewal, dressed up as a bill?

C28.name: Relationship plausibility (fits the customer's business?)
C28.description: Does this purchase fit the customer's business and normal suppliers? A landscaper buying aviation surveys is odd.
C28.plain: Would your business normally buy this? A landscaper paying for aviation surveys is odd.

C29.name: Spelling / formatting quality
C29.description: Spelling and formatting quality compared with a professional invoice. Weak on its own.
C29.plain: Is it as polished as a real business invoice? A weak signal on its own.

C30.name: Lookalike domain (dnstwist-style)
C30.description: Looks for email or web domains one letter off the real supplier's (tallowoodmulch vs tallowwoodmulch).
C30.plain: Is the email or website one letter off the real supplier's?

C31.name: Domain age (RDAP; for .au use crt.sh / Wayback)
C31.description: How old the sender's domain is, from certificate and web-archive history. Days-old domains are a red flag.
C31.plain: How old is the sender's website? Days-old websites are a red flag.

C32.name: .au registrant eligibility ID ≠ invoice ABN
C32.description: For .au domains, checks the registrant's ABN matches the ABN on the invoice.
C32.plain: For .au websites, is it registered to the same ABN as the invoice?

C33.name: Email DNS posture (MX/SPF/DMARC)
C33.description: Email security setup (MX, SPF, DMARC) on the sender's domain. Missing records make spoofing easier.
C33.plain: Is the sender's email properly set up so it's hard to fake?

C34.name: Official contact details cross-check
C34.description: Finds the supplier's official contact details independently and compares them with the invoice.
C34.plain: Find the supplier's real contact details independently and compare them with the invoice.

C35.name: Web presence / scam reports
C35.description: Searches for reviews, an established web presence, and scam reports about the business.
C35.plain: Does the business have reviews and a real web presence, or scam reports?

C36.name: ASIC company status
C36.description: Checks ASIC: is the company registered, and is it deregistered or in administration?
C36.plain: Is the company still registered, or deregistered or in administration?

C37.name: Logo provenance
C37.description: Checks whether the logo was lifted from the real supplier's website.
C37.plain: Was the logo copied from the real supplier's website?

C38.name: Render-vs-text OCR forensics on payment fields
C38.description: Compares what the page shows with the text hidden underneath, to catch payment fields that render differently from their text.
C38.plain_name: What you see vs what's underneath
C38.plain: Does the page show different bank details from the text hidden underneath?

C39.name: Prior-revision recovery ("original details were…")
C39.description: Recovers the original bank details from earlier versions inside the PDF, so the report can say "the real account was…".
C39.plain: Dig out the original bank details from earlier versions inside the PDF.

C40.name: Director / officeholder checks
C40.description: Checks directors and officeholders for links to known scams or phoenix companies.
C40.plain: Are the company's directors linked to known scams or failed companies?

C41.name: Human call-back / fraud-team referral
C41.description: Hands the case to a person: a call-back on a known number or a fraud-team referral.
C41.plain: Hand it to a person: call the supplier on a known number or refer to the fraud team.

C42.name: Embedded payment link or QR destination
C42.description: Extracts links and QR destinations without opening them and checks whether they conflict with the supplier or printed payment details.
C42.plain: Where do the payment links or QR codes really go? Checked without opening them.

C43.name: Account-name and entity-type mismatch
C43.description: Checks whether a personal payee name is being used for a company supplier, or the payee is otherwise unrelated to the registered entity.
C43.plain_name: Personal name on a company account
C43.plain: Is a company being paid into a personal account, or one unrelated to the business?

C44.name: Invoice chronology anomaly
C44.description: Detects future issue dates, due dates before issue dates and implausibly stale invoices.
C44.plain: Is it dated in the future, due before it was issued, or very old?

C47.name: Cross-customer payee reuse or mule pattern
C47.description: Detects one new account appearing for multiple unrelated suppliers or customers in fictional bank-side observations.
C47.plain: Is this new account turning up for several unrelated suppliers? A sign of a money-mule account.

C48.name: Template reuse across unrelated suppliers
C48.description: Uses layout fingerprints to find the same invoice template presented as unrelated suppliers.
C48.plain: Is the same invoice layout being used by businesses that should be unrelated?

C50.name: Supplier domain changed from history
C50.description: Detects a newly seen email domain for a known supplier even when it is not a spelling lookalike.
C50.plain: Is a known supplier suddenly emailing from a different domain?

C51.name: Currency or geography mismatch
C51.description: Flags foreign currency or payment geography inconsistent with a domestic supplier and customer history.
C51.plain: Is a local supplier suddenly asking for foreign currency or an overseas account?

C52.name: BPAY biller and CRN consistency
C52.description: Validates biller identity and customer-reference rules when reliable bank-side BPAY data is available.
C52.plain: Are the BPAY biller code and reference number valid for this biller?
